title.title: The optimal quartic separation of randomized and quantum queries
title.subtitle: Claim: total functions with $R \ge Q^{4-o(1)}$, so the known $R = O(Q^4)$ is optimal

beats.text: How far can quantum queries beat randomized ones on total functions?
Separations crept up to $3 - o(1)$, and a cubic upper bound was conjectured
Claim: $4 - o(1)$, matching the known $R = O(Q^4)$: the exponent is exactly 4

after.label: Claimed, 5 Oct 2026
after.note: total Boolean functions, up to polylog factors

achievement.note: Disproves the conjectured $R = O(Q^3)$; with $R = O(Q^4)$ the exponent is 4

verify.detail: No formalization; 19 pages that query-complexity experts can check quickly
verify.ourCheck: We read the papers' claims and caveats; we did not referee them

sources.quote: Aaronson-Ben-David-Kothari-Rao-Tal (STOC 2021), via Huang's sensitivity theorem, proved D=O(Q^4) and conjectured R=O(Q^3)

plain: How much can quantum computers save when they answer by peeking at inputs? Up to the fourth power, exactly

steps: Start from Forrelation: easy for quantum, hard for random guessing
Add a cheat sheet whose address it computes, checked by pointers
The full function keeps the gap, nearly to the fourth power

voice.text: Separations crept up to cubic, and cubic was conjectured to be the limit.
Wrap Forrelation in a pointer cheat sheet; the total function keeps the advantage.
Claimed: nearly quartic, so the exponent is four.
